findings.title: join() treats timeout=0 as no timeout
findings.body: SpanFlusher.join computes deadline as `time.time() + timeout if timeout else None`. If a caller passes timeout=0, which should mean non-blocking join, the expression is falsy and deadline becomes None, so join can block indefinitely. Use `if timeout is not None`.

findings.title: join() can return while flusher processes are still running
findings.body: SpanFlusher.join uses one deadline for both `next_step.join(timeout)` and waiting on child processes. If the downstream join consumes most or all of the timeout, the remaining-time check breaks out of the process loop and later flusher processes are never terminated. Since the stopped flag is only checked between flush iterations, a process blocked in Redis or Kafka work can outlive join, leaking processes and potentially continuing to flush after a rebalance.

findings.title: unhealthy flusher processes are replaced without reaping the old process
findings.body: In `_ensure_processes_alive`, a dead or killed process is replaced immediately by `_create_process_for_shards` without joining or otherwise reaping the old Process object. For multiprocessing children this can leave zombie processes and file descriptors, and because the old process is not waited on after kill, there is a window where the replacement may start before the old child has fully exited. Repeated restarts can leak process-table resources.

findings.title: added sleep in test is disabled by monkeypatch
findings.body: test_basic monkeypatches `time.sleep` to a no-op, then calls `time.sleep(0.1)` to give flusher threads time to observe the changed drift. Because the monkeypatch is active, this call does not actually wait, so the test remains timing-dependent and may be racy. Use a real wait condition or avoid patching the sleep used for synchronization.

findings.title: --flusher-processes 0 unexpectedly spawns one process per shard
findings.body: SpanFlusher initializes `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, so a value of 0 is treated as unset. The new `--flusher-processes` CLI option is an unvalidated int, so passing 0 will not disable or limit processes; it will fall back to spawning one process per assigned shard. Validate positive values or use `if max_processes is None`.
